strengths: Honest and rigorous reporting of a negative result — the paper clearly characterizes why conformal risk control achieves the safety guarantee but fails to deliver practical speedup, which is itself a useful finding for the community
Principled theoretical framing using the Waudby-Smith-Ramdas betting bound provides finite-sample guarantees without retraining, which is a real practical advantage over learned stopping policies
The root-cause diagnosis (answer-stability signal too weak; draft answers stabilize only after most context is processed) is actionable and informative for future work on memory agent efficiency
weaknesses: Practical utility is essentially zero — a 1.02–1.14× speedup is indistinguishable from no speedup, raising the question of whether this constitutes a publishable contribution beyond a null result

The answer-stability stopping rule appears naive and under-motivated; the paper does not explain why this signal was selected over alternatives (e.g., confidence-based, entropy-based), making it unclear whether the failure is fundamental to conformal risk control or just to this particular stopping signal
Experimental scope is narrow: only one memory agent (MemAgent), two context lengths, and 8 configurations — insufficient to generalize the negative finding across the broader class of memory agents
The contributions section explicitly frames a failure to achieve practical speedup as a contribution, which weakens the overall impact claim and risks framing negative results as positive ones

ai_detection.reasoning: The introduction follows a textbook funnel structure (problem → gap → method → results → contributions) with no deviation or discursive voice. The three-bullet contribution list with parallel syntactic structure is a near-universal AI writing pattern. Prose is uniformly clean and precise without the tonal variation, hedging qualifications, or narrative idiosyncrasies typical of human academic writing.
